title: Matching Attacks for Multi-User Double Encryption
summary: The bound is tight when n is at least k, including DES and AES; matching attacks remain open when n is much smaller than k.

formal_statement.body: In the multi-user security setting for double encryption, the security bound is tight when $n \geq k$, including the DES and AES settings; when $n \ll k$, a regime occurring in Format-Preserving Encryption and several block-cipher designs, the unresolved task is to find attacks whose advantage matches the applicable bound.

scope.domain: Multi-user security and attack discovery for double encryption in symmetric cryptography.
parameters: n and k (parameters compared to determine the applicable bound regime)
scope.unresolved_remainder: Find attacks whose advantage matches the applicable bound when n is much smaller than k.

citations.label: The Multi-user Security of Double Encryption

progress.summary: The source notes that the bound is tight when n is at least k, including DES and AES. It explicitly leaves finding matching attacks when n is much smaller than k as an open problem.
citation_labels: Viet Tung Hoang et al., The Multi-user Security of Double Encryption
